_readme: Editorial phrase bank for the Editorial Footprint Risk (EFR) system.
READ docs/editorial-footprint-research-2026-08-26.md BEFORE EDITING. Every
class below has a different evidence standard and a different CI role, and
the differences are the whole point of the file.
THIS IS NOT AN AI-DETECTION LIST. No entry here is evidence that any page
was machine-written, and no output of this system may be phrased that way.
Population-level studies that establish these markers explicitly disclaim
per-document inference, and roughly a third of English web pages published
since 2023 carry at least one of them.
Every entry was measured against this site's own corpus before being
written down. `corpusFrequency` and `pageFrequency` are occurrences and
distinct indexable EN pages as of `lastReviewed`; `variety` is distinct
containing sentences divided by pages, and it decides the FIX:
variety near 0 -> one shared string on many pages. Fix the TEMPLATE.
variety near 1+ -> written many different times. Fix the WRITING.
A rule aimed at the wrong one of those asks hundreds of pages to hand-edit
a string that has a single source.
Entries with corpusFrequency 0 are deliberate and legitimate: they are
FORWARD-LOOKING guards against constructions this site does not currently
use and should not start using. They are recorded with their real measured
zero rather than with a borrowed reputation.
Do not add an entry unilaterally, and never to make a page pass. Same bar
as data/translation_parity_exceptions.json and data/english_parent_exceptions.json.

corpusBasis.note: Counts are from scripts/mine-editorial-phrases.js over the whole tree, indexable pages only. Regenerate with `npm run mine:editorial-phrases`.

forbidden.meaning: Should not appear in newly written or newly edited user-facing editorial prose.
forbidden.ciRole: blocking on introduction only, never on pre-existing text
forbidden.evidenceStandard: deterministic and unambiguous, or an explicit house style decision

strongly_discouraged.meaning: A formulaic construction that carries no information. Rewrite as the fact it is standing in for.
strongly_discouraged.evidenceStandard: corpus evidence here, or a population-level finding recorded as such

density_limited.meaning: Legitimate in small numbers; a footprint at concentration. Scored as a rate, never as presence.
density_limited.evidenceStandard: population-level vocabulary studies plus a locally calibrated cap

search_protected.meaning: Repeats because it is the product, the user's job, or the query. EXEMPT from all density scoring.
search_protected.ciRole: removal from a page that ranks for it is a blocking SEO-preservation failure
search_protected.evidenceStandard: product terminology or observed query language

exemptionTypes.subject: The page is ABOUT this character or term (matched against its slug, title and H1). symbol/em-dash is titled 'Em Dash (—): Copy & Paste + Why It Became the "AI Writing" Tell' and necessarily contains 27 em dashes.
exemptionTypes.family: Page families where the pattern is inherent to the content type.
exemptionTypes.locale: Locales where the pattern is grammatically normal or required.

entries.rationale: House style decision for this site, adopted on a population-level signal and NOT as a claim about any page. Em dash frequency on the web roughly doubled after 2023 and one measurement puts a current model at ~3.3x a human baseline; the same reporting is explicit that spotting machine text this way is 'more art than science'. The rule is therefore about how this site chooses to write, not about what any page is.
entries.replacementGuidance: A colon when what follows explains what precedes; a full stop when it is a separate thought; a comma pair for a genuine aside; parentheses for a true parenthetical. If none of those fits, the sentence is doing two jobs and should be two sentences.
entries.notes: FORWARD-ONLY for pages a branch leaves alone, and that half is not negotiable: 52,766 occurrences on 98.9% of pages is a total backlog, and Google's own guidance warns against quick-fix element removal and against changing content that already performs. REVISED 2026-09-02 (user direction) - CLEAN-ON-TOUCH for the rest. A page whose own copy a branch edits (title, meta description, H1, headings, prose or FAQ text changed since the merge base) must leave with zero em dashes in every measured slot, cards included; the gate reports those as `em-dash-touched`. An English page that is touched pulls its locale siblings along (`em-dash-sibling`). Existing em dashes are still never auto-edited, and an untouched page is still only reported. The subject exemption is load-bearing: without it this rule flags the site's own em-dash page.

entries.pattern: \b(?:as an AI|as a large language model|I(?:'m| am) an AI|my (?:training data|knowledge cutoff)|as of my last update)\b
entries.rationale: Assistant self-reference in published page copy is contamination, not style. There is no editorial reading under which a page should say this to a reader.
entries.replacementGuidance: Delete. If the sentence was hedging a fact, verify the fact and state it.
entries.notes: Measured zero on the live corpus. The one apparent hit was symbol/em-dash, whose title discusses the 'AI writing tell' claim as its subject — which is why this entry carries a subject exemption rather than being a bare string match.

entries.rationale: An unrendered template variable or an unfilled placeholder shipped to a reader is a build defect. Deterministic, zero legitimate occurrences.
entries.replacementGuidance: Fill it in, or fix the generator that failed to.
entries.notes: Code, <kbd> and <pre> are removed before this runs, so a documented template syntax inside a code sample cannot trip it. Split 2026-09-01: the bare TODO/FIXME/TBD tokens moved to EFR-F-005, which is case-sensitive. They cannot live here because this entry needs case-insensitivity for "lorem ipsum" and "[insert name]", and under that flag "TODO" also matches the ordinary Spanish and Portuguese word "todo".

entries.rationale: An unfilled placeholder token shipped to a reader is a build defect. Matched case-sensitively because the all-caps form is the only one that is a placeholder: lowercase "todo" is an everyday Spanish and Portuguese word, and "tbd" appears inside ordinary text.
entries.replacementGuidance: Fill it in, or fix the generator that failed to.
entries.notes: Split out of EFR-F-003 on 2026-09-01 because that entry compiles with the i flag. Measured over every indexable page: case-insensitively this pattern matched 511 times on 301 pages, all of them the Spanish and Portuguese word "todo" (211 es, 90 pt) and zero of them a real placeholder. JavaScript \b is ASCII-only, so it also fired inside accented words such as "metodo" with an accent. Case-sensitively it matches 0 pages, and still catches a real all-caps TODO. model-leakage is blocking-eligible, so left as it was this rule would have blocked every PR touching any of those 301 pages the day the gate left shadow mode.

entries.pattern: \b(?:Here(?:'s| is) (?:a|an|the) (?:comprehensive|detailed|revised|updated|rewritten|complete)|Certainly[,!]|I hope this helps|Feel free to (?:let me know|reach out)|In conclusion,)\b
entries.rationale: Conversational scaffolding addressed to a commissioner rather than a reader. A page is not a reply.
entries.replacementGuidance: Delete the wrapper and keep the content. If deleting it leaves nothing, there was nothing.
entries.notes: English only. The equivalent scaffolding in other languages needs its own corpus evidence before an entry exists — translating this pattern would be exactly the bias the research memo §6 forbids.

entries.rationale: The strongest genuine editorial habit found on this site: 218 occurrences across 154 EN pages, at variety ~1.0, meaning it was written afresh each time rather than inherited from one template. It asserts fit without naming the property that produces the fit.
entries.evidenceSource: corpus mining 2026-08-26 ('great for' 159/106 pages, variety 0.92; 'perfect for' 40/30, variety 1.30; 'ideal for' 19/18, variety 1.06)
entries.replacementGuidance: Name the property. 'Great for Instagram bios' -> 'Fits the 150-character Instagram bio limit'. 'Perfect for Discord' -> 'Survives Discord's Markdown parser unchanged'.
entries.notes: Variety ~1.0 across all three variants is what makes this an editorial rule and not a template fix.

entries.pattern: \b(?:not just\b[^.!?]{2,60}?\b(?:but|it(?:'|’)s|they(?:'|’)re)|not only\b[^.!?]{2,60}?\bbut|more than just\b|less about\b[^.!?]{2,50}?\bmore about\b|it(?:'|’)s not\b[^.!?]{2,50}?[,;]\s*it(?:'|’)s\b)
entries.rationale: Negative parallelism manufactures contrast without adding information: the reader learns what the thing is not, which they were not wondering. A large Common Crawl analysis reports this construction nearly TRIPLED on the web after 2023.
entries.replacementGuidance: Delete the negative half and keep the positive claim, then make the positive claim specific. 'Not just a font changer but a full toolkit' -> 'Converts to 114 Unicode styles and checks each against seven platforms' limits'.
entries.notes: FORWARD-LOOKING. Only 5 occurrences on 5 pages here, so this rule currently protects rather than repairs. Recorded with its measured near-zero, not with the reputation the construction has elsewhere.

entries.pattern: ^\s*(?:in today(?:'|’)s|in the world of|in an era|at its core|when it comes to|let(?:'|’)s (?:dive|explore)|it(?:'|’)s (?:worth|important) (?:noting|to note)|it is (?:worth|important) (?:noting|to note))\b
entries.rationale: Sentence openers that delay the answer. The reader arrived with a question; the first clause should answer it.
entries.evidenceSource: corpus mining 2026-08-26 — measured 0 occurrences across 904 indexable EN pages
entries.replacementGuidance: Start with the answer. The answers/ family already does this and its 'Short answer' block is the house pattern worth copying.
entries.notes: FORWARD-LOOKING, and the measured zero is the finding: the widely-cited opener list simply does not describe this site. Kept as a guard because these are cheap to introduce and hard to notice once shipped.

entries.pattern: ^\s*(?:whether you(?:'|’)?(?:re| are)?|looking for|if you(?:'|’)?(?:re| are) looking)\b
entries.rationale: The audience-enumerating opener ('Whether you're a student, a designer, or a gamer…') addresses everyone and informs no one, and it costs the first sentence — the one a snippet is most likely to take.
entries.evidenceSource: corpus mining 2026-08-26 ('whether you' 50 occurrences / 48 pages, variety 1.00; 'looking for' 30/27, variety 1.00)
entries.replacementGuidance: Pick the one reader this page is actually for and tell them the fact they came for.
entries.notes: Scoped to sentence-initial position on purpose: 'whether you use Windows or macOS' mid-sentence is a real distinction and is not matched.

entries.rationale: Unsupported benefit adjectives and verbs. Individually ordinary English; at concentration they are the signature of copy written to sound valuable rather than to be informative. Population-level vocabulary studies find style-affecting verbs and adjectives, not content nouns, are what surged post-2023.
entries.evidenceSource: docs/editorial-footprint-research-2026-08-26.md §4.1; corpus mining 2026-08-26 (11 occurrences / 9 EN pages combined)
entries.replacementGuidance: State the observable behaviour instead. 'Seamlessly works across platforms' -> 'Pastes unchanged into Discord, Instagram and LinkedIn; Twitter strips the variation selector'.
entries.notes: A RATE, never a presence test. One 'versatile' on a 900-word page is nothing; six is a voice. The cap is calibrated in docs/editorial-footprint-calibration-2026-08-26.md and is per-locale.

entries.rationale: The excess-vocabulary set identified by measuring >15 million biomedical abstracts before and after 2022: 379 excess style words in 2024, ~66% verbs and ~14% adjectives. Included as a density signal precisely as the source frames it — a corpus-level marker, not per-document evidence.
entries.notes: Deliberately excludes the noun 'underscore' — on this site that is the CHARACTER _, appearing 169 times across 65 pages inside factual platform username rules ('lowercase a-z, 0-9, underscores and periods only'). Only the verb phrase 'underscores the' is matched. Banning the bare word would have deleted facts from every username-rules page; see EFR-S-004.

entries.pattern: \b(?:stand(?:s|ing)? out|designed to|built to|crafted to|easy to use|user[- ]friendly|makes? it easy|take[s]? (?:your|it) [^.!?]{0,25}to the next level)\b
entries.rationale: Purpose and outcome claims with no measurable content. Present but not pervasive here, and legitimate in small numbers — 'stand out' is genuinely part of the user's job on a decorative-text site, which is why this is a cap rather than a ban.
entries.evidenceSource: corpus mining 2026-08-26 ('stand out' 125 occurrences / 66 pages, variety 1.76; 'designed/built/crafted to' 37/27, variety 1.33; 'easy to use' 1/1)
entries.replacementGuidance: Replace the claim with the mechanism: 'makes your bio stand out' -> 'renders in a script style Instagram keeps intact, unlike the default font'.
entries.notes: seoProtection: watch. 'stand out' appears inside real FAQ questions users ask ('How do I make my New Year message stand out?'), so the faqQuestions slot is exempt — a question is the user's words, not ours.

entries.rationale: The site's core job and its highest-volume query family. 1,181 occurrences across 602 of 904 indexable EN pages at variety 1.34 — high frequency AND high variety, which is what genuine subject language looks like as opposed to a template.
entries.replacementGuidance: None. Do not replace this with a synonym to lower a score. Removing it from a page that ranks for it is a blocking SEO-preservation failure.
entries.notes: Exempt from every density measure. Google's spam policy names 'automated transformations like synonymizing' as scaled content abuse, so synonym-swapping the site's own head term is the worst available move.

entries.rationale: The subject matter. 4,261 occurrences across 776 EN pages at variety 3.43 — the highest variety of any frequent term measured, i.e. written differently almost every time.
entries.notes: Language-independent: 'Unicode' is a proper noun and is cited by that name in every locale here.

entries.rationale: Head-term query language. 'font generator' 311 occurrences / 113 pages (variety 1.93); 'fancy text' 141/42 (2.57); 'bold text' 129/62 (1.35); 'text generator' 188/60 (2.52). All high variety.
entries.notes: The EN homepage's own H1 is 'Fancy Text Generator'; a ratified local-only exception in CLAUDE.md turns on that fact. Never substitute these.

entries.rationale: Character and Unicode terminology. These are the names of the things this site documents, and several collide head-on with marker lists: 'underscore' appears 169 times across 65 pages as the character _ in factual platform username rules, and would be deleted by a naive ban on the LLM verb 'underscore'.
entries.evidenceSource: corpus scan 2026-08-26; context inspection of all 65 'underscore' pages
entries.replacementGuidance: None. These are formal identifiers; translating or substituting one breaks the page.
entries.pluralNote: Every term carries its plural. The first version did not, and `\bunderscore\b` does not match "underscores" — which is the form the username-rules pages actually use ("letters, numbers and underscores only"), so the protection missed the exact case it was written for. Found by test, not by reading.
entries.notes: Same principle CLAUDE.md's 'a formal identifier is not English' rule already applies to the locale-translation gate, applied here to the phrase bank.

entries.rationale: Platform, game and product entity names. They are the entities pages are retrieved for, and entity coverage is what the SEO Preservation Gate protects.
entries.replacementGuidance: None. Dropping a platform name from a page that ranks for it is a blocking SEO-preservation failure, not a style improvement.
entries.notes: Also counts toward the specificity dimension: naming a platform and stating its actual behaviour is concrete information.

_readme: NOT phrase-bank entries, and deliberately so. These are single strings
reproduced verbatim across many pages by a template or generator. They are
recorded here because a phrase rule is the WRONG instrument for them: the
fix is one edit upstream, not N edits downstream, and a per-page warning
would ask hundreds of pages to each repair one shared source.
`variety` is distinct containing sentences divided by pages. Everything
here is far below 1.
Owners and the upstream fix for each are in
docs/editorial-footprint-upstream-findings-2026-08-26.md.

strings.text: Transform text with Unicode fonts / Use UltraTextGen to convert plain text into…
strings.note: This single card is the entire reason the word 'transform' scores 911 occurrences on 443 pages. Treating 'transform' as a marker word would have been a pure false positive.

strings.text: Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
Everything runs in your browser — no app or sign-up.
strings.note: Also carries an em dash, so one upstream edit clears 184 pages of EFR-F-001 backlog at once. This is the highest-leverage single fix on the site.

strings.text: Copy a full combo in one click and paste it into a bio, caption, or username.
Choosing "Save as PDF" in the same dialog gives you a PDF instead of paper.
Use / Print this letter … / Download PNG to save it …
Yes — every letter A–Z has its own bubble page.
